dossiers.thesis_summary: Annexon reads out the Month 15 primary endpoint of the Phase 3 ARCHER II trial of vonaprument in geographic atrophy in Q4 2026 — a dated, forward, unfired, idiosyncratic trial readout, reconfirmed in the 12-Aug-2026 Q2 release and on the 19-Aug earnings call. The endpoint is BCVA >=15-letter loss, a functional VISION endpoint, which is what makes the asset differentiated: both approved GA drugs (Apellis SYFOVRE, Astellas Izervay) are anatomical lesion-growth agents with no demonstrated vision benefit, and fewer than 10% of diagnosed GA patients are treated today. Behind the GA event sits a second, largely independent asset — tanruprubart in Guillain-Barre syndrome, BLA submission guided for Q4 2026 with an EU MAA under EMA review since Jan-2026, which would be the first approved disease-modifying therapy in an indication with ~150,000 cases/yr and zero approved options. The structure of the trade changed materially on 12-Aug-2026, when the company added a Month 24 dual primary endpoint (independent timepoint, 2027) plus an open-label extension: a Month 15 miss is no longer terminal, and the 30-Jul-2026 Oxford Finance facility (up to $200M, $50M drawn) plus $209.2M of cash funds the company to reach that second shot. Both the board's win leg and the skeptic's floor were derived before these facts and are corrected below.
dossiers.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that a positive Month 15 BCVA result is genuinely achievable and that the Month 24 dual primary is a real second shot rather than a tell. The live record pushes back hard. Adding a Month 24 primary endpoint in the final quarter before an M15 readout, announced in the same release as an OLE launch and two weeks after drawing $50M of senior secured debt, is the pattern of a sponsor building a landing pad; the market read it that way and marked the stock down ~6%, and analysts on the 19-Aug call pressed management directly on whether it signalled concern about M15 (management said M15 remains the base case). Substantively: neither approved GA drug has ever shown a functional vision benefit, and vonaprument's own vision signal comes from a Phase 2 (ARCHER) that MISSED its primary anatomical endpoint — the prospective functional endpoint is unproven in this mechanism and this class. Second residual: my $2.85 floor is a modelled intrinsic, not an observed clearing price. The 52-week low of $2.10 was printed on a weaker balance sheet but also a cleaner setup, and a post-miss print in the low $2s or below is entirely plausible before the market gives the M24 shot or the GBS asset any credit — small-cap biotech overshoots through intrinsic on a failed pivotal. Treat $2.85 as the funded intrinsic and the low $2s as the tape risk.

dossiers.thesis_summary: Signed all-cash merger: Aquarian Capital acquires Brighthouse at $70.00/share (~$4.1bn), agreement 6 Nov 2025, shareholder-adopted 12 Feb 2026, HSR expired. Every closing condition is satisfied or waived except acquisition-of-control approvals from the Delaware, New York and Massachusetts insurance regulators (plus FINRA for Brighthouse Securities). The deal did NOT close by its original 6 September 2026 outside date; the merger agreement's automatic extension has triggered because regulatory approvals were the sole unmet condition, pushing the termination right to 6 December 2026. No termination has been filed or announced. The binding gate is the Delaware Form A / Chapter 50 review of Brighthouse Life Insurance Company: as of the Department's 17 August 2026 statement it had retained outside actuaries, auditors and investigators, and had NOT noticed the statutorily required public hearing. At $53.58 the spread is 23.5% wide against a signed, shareholder-approved contract — the market is pricing roughly even odds of a Delaware denial or an Aquarian walk, not a capped arb.
dossiers.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the Dec-6 extension keeps Aquarian on the hook at $70. It does not. Dec 6 is a termination RIGHT exercisable by EITHER party, not a self-executing deadline and not a commitment device — the extension bought calendar, not obligation. If Delaware signals it will condition approval on incremental capital at Brighthouse Reinsurance Company of Delaware, Aquarian can simply let 6 December pass and walk; nothing in the record establishes a reverse termination fee large enough to compel closing, and Aquarian's own financing backdrop sits under the same AM Best under-review-with-negative-implications umbrella (reaffirmed 29 July 2026). Second, my $45 floor assumes a break returns BHF to a peer-drift-marked unaffected price. A break caused by a Delaware DENIAL would not be a clean return: it stamps a public regulatory verdict on the affiliate-reinsurance capital structure that the Capitol Forum flagged on 7 August 2026, which is NEW adverse standalone information, and it simultaneously removes the private-capital bid pool for this balance sheet. In that specific branch the floor is $41 (~0.49x the $84.35 book, ~0.26x the $156.10 book ex-AOCI), which cuts R:R from 1.91 to 1.31 and lifts the market-implied close probability to 43.4% — within a point of my own 45% estimate, i.e. the edge goes to roughly zero. Third, the calendar itself is the quiet killer: with no hearing noticed and ~89 days left, a Delaware notice-hearing-decision sequence must begin by roughly mid-to-late October to land inside the window at all.

dossiers.thesis_summary: Dingdong (Cayman) has a signed 5-Feb-2026 SPA to sell its China business to Two Hearts Investments Limited, a wholly owned Meituan subsidiary, for US$717m cash struck off the 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet, on top of which the listed parent was permitted to draw up to US$280m of cash out of the China group pre-closing (the company's own "up to US$997m" framing). Shareholders approved both the SPA and the capital-return authority on 27 Mar 2026; there is no financing contingency. Verified live on 2026-09-08: the extraction is substantially done (US$267.1m of cash and short-term investments at the parent at 30 Jun 2026 versus RMB45.7m at 31 Dec 2025) and the deal is unfired — the most recent SEC filing of any type for CIK 0001854545 is the 21 Aug 2026 6-K, which still names SAMR anti-monopoly clearance as an outstanding closing condition. Second and independent: even on close, the cash reaching ADS holders is a permission rather than an obligation — AGM Resolution 2 authorises a return "at such time, in such manner as the Board, in its absolute discretion, deems appropriate" — while the consideration is expressly "subject to adjustments based on certain net cash, net working capital and other financial line items ... as of certain agreed upon dates" plus a leakage deduction, and 10% of it is payable only after the Company settles PRC taxes on the transaction, including the non-resident indirect-transfer filings that are themselves a closing condition. So both the amount and the arrival are contingent, and neither has a date attached.

Verified live and unfired as of 8 September 2026: the 6 August 2026 second-quarter release confirmed enrollment and dosing complete across all dose levels including the four-week treatment period and four-week safety follow-up, and reaffirmed the readout as anticipated in the second half of 2026. Identical guidance appeared on 7 May 2026, so the timeline has not slipped. It is a guidance WINDOW, not a date: no venue, no presentation slot, no regulatory deadline, nothing contractually owed on any day; the company controls both timing and framing and the window runs to 31 December 2026. The January 2026 interim was a partial slice (roughly 85 percent median CRP reduction at four weeks, 94 percent of subjects below 2 mg/L); the complete dataset, the full dose range and the calprotectin biomarker are still unreleased, so the edge is unspent. The event is idiosyncratic — it resolves on the company's own trial data. What has changed since the board struck this dossier on 8 June 2026 is the underwriting basis, not the event: on 31 July 2026 Novo Nordisk's Phase 3 ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab (IL-6 antibody, over 6,300 ASCVD/CKD patients with hsCRP >= 2 mg/L) missed its primary endpoint with a hazard ratio of 0.99 (95% CI 0.88-1.11) despite confirmed target engagement and the expected free-IL-6 and hsCRP reductions, with more serious infections than placebo. GFORCE-1 reports the same class of biomarker that ZEUS just showed does not predict outcomes. The catalyst remains live, but its power to force a re-rating in the atherosclerotic cardiovascular indication is substantially impaired, and every valuation axis on this record has to be re-cut ex-ASCVD.

(1) ZEUS proved that suppressing precisely the biomarker GFORCE-1 reports (free IL-6 / hsCRP) does not translate into outcomes, so a clean CRP result invites a shrug or an outright sell-the-news. (2) The market has already seen the punchline: the January 2026 interim showed roughly 85 percent median CRP reduction and 94 percent of subjects below 2 mg/L, and the stock is nonetheless down 42 percent since 1 July. The full dataset is confirmatory, not revelatory. (3) The company is still guiding a Phase 2 in elevated atherosclerotic risk and cardiometabolic syndrome in H2 2026 — post-ZEUS that reads as capital allocation into a refuted hypothesis and can be taken negatively on the same day the data print. (4) There is no forcing function: $626.0M funds operations into 2029 and the lead wholly-owned asset is Phase 1, so management can release this as a poster or a conference slide at a time of its choosing with no obligation to frame it as an event at all. A soft, undated, self-published biomarker readout in a mechanism the tape has just discounted is the weakest form of catalyst on this board.

So the panel's negative vote was on a question the company is no longer asking, and the FDA chose to extend rather than act on 22 August. The pipeline gave me exactly one survivor this run, so this concentration is an intake fact as much as a choice.

EXPRESSION IS THE WHOLE RISK CONTROL HERE. RARE is valuation_method=binary_prob, so equity is barred and defined risk is mandatory — which is fortunate, because equity is the wrong structure for this file on its own merits. The gross equity payoff is 1.08:1 (+20.9% win, -19.3% lose); the entire edge is the 0.75 probability, not the asymmetry, and the $12.35 floor is soft — only ~$1.77/share of already-earned GENGLYCOS voucher is non-contingent, and a floor of identical construction (the board's $18.00) broke by 25% in a single session on 3 September.
